_meta.purpose: Canonical AWS-service -> GCP-service classification (the 'logical construct'). Single source of truth used by service_classifier.py to force the correct GCP target and eliminate LLM label variance. Grounded in Google's official 'Google Cloud for AWS professionals' service comparison. Curate this file to add/adjust services.

mode_semantics.keep: Pipeline already prices this well deterministically — classifier only STAMPS metadata (category/reason), never changes pricing or the mapped SKU.
mode_semantics.review: Correct GCP target is known but precise GCP pricing needs per-service modelling. Classifier FORCES gcp_service=target + strategy=passthrough (carry AWS cost, no invented figure) + manual-review flag. Honest baseline until a deterministic pricer is built.
mode_semantics.ignore: Not a real workload cost on GCP (burstable CPU credits, billing fees, taxes, support, refunds). Classifier FORCES strategy='ignore' -> $0. GCP has no equivalent charge.

_meta.match: Case-insensitive substring against the AWS product name with the leading 'Amazon '/'AWS ' stripped. First match wins, so order specific -> general.
_meta.field_order_note: Downstream row metadata stored as: category, gcp_service, confidence, rule='service_map_v1', reason (in projection_note).

rules.match: relational database service for mysql community edition
rules.reason: RDS Extended Support (MySQL Community Edition EOL surcharge). AWS charges per vCPU-hour for running MySQL 5.7 past its EOL date. Cloud SQL has no equivalent surcharge — customers on older MySQL versions pay standard rates. This cost disappears entirely on GCP.

CloudTrail charges per recorded management/data event; Cloud Logging charges primarily by ingested log volume — a direct event-count-to-log-volume conversion has no reliable basis without knowing average event size, retention, exclusions, and sink configuration. Passthrough at AWS cost until a real CloudTrail-specific sizing model exists; architecture review recommended.

CloudWatch is multi-component (metrics + logs + alarms + dashboards). PutLogEvents (log ingestion) is priced directly: Cloud Logging Log Ingestion at near cost parity ($0.50/GB AWS vs $0.50/GiB GCP = ~7% cheaper on GCP). Other sub-components (metric API calls, alarms, dashboards) remain passthrough until per-unit pricers are built.
Cloud NAT: gateway-hours (Private Nat Gateway Uptime) + data processed (Cloud Nat Data Processing), each priced by its own real SKU.
Cloud NAT: gateway-hours + data processed.
AWS Config has no 1:1 GCP equivalent (partial: Asset Inventory).
Managed Hadoop/Spark -> Dataproc; priced by cluster node hours (Dataproc Premium vCPU-hour rate for management-fee rows, or an honest passthrough for spot/storage/backup rows).
Serverless ETL -> Dataflow (or Cloud Data Fusion).
Serverless query -> BigQuery on-demand (per TB scanned).
Data warehouse -> BigQuery (or BigQuery editions/Dataproc).
Streaming -> Pub/Sub (or Managed Kafka for KDS-heavy).
MSK -> self-hosted Kafka on GCE; LLM maps to GCE instance family — preserving instance-level mapping.
MSK -> self-hosted Kafka on GCE; LLM maps to GCE instance family.
No managed GCP equivalent; LLM maps to self-hosted GCE — preserving instance-level mapping.
No managed GCP equivalent; LLM maps to self-hosted GCE.

BI -> Looker Studio Pro. AWS QuickSight usage_type strings encode role/edition directly (Author vs Reader, Standard vs Enterprise/Pro) and the CUR quantity for these usage types IS the per-user/session count -- a deterministic static mapper (map_quicksight) now converts Author seats to Looker Studio Pro's published $9/user/mo; Reader/session and Q-Topic rows still passthrough (see map_quicksight docstring).

Amazon Q Developer/Business is AWS's own first-party GenAI assistant -- a real AWS service, not third-party Marketplace SaaS (confirmed real: raw product code 'AmazonQ' has no space after 'Amazon', so it was falling through classify_mechanics.py's marketplace_thirdparty catch-all, which only excludes rows canonical_service() recognizes). Nearest GCP equivalent confirmed via the same live-catalog-sweep methodology used elsewhere: searched catalog.duckdb for a per-seat Code Assist/subscription SKU -- none exists (only per-token 'Gemini API' usage SKUs are exposed via the public Cloud Billing Catalog API this pipeline's catalog is built from). Gemini Code Assist Standard's published seat price ($19/user/mo) is exact parity with this row's own usage_type ('Amazon-Q-Developer-Pro-subscription-monthly', AWS's published Q Developer Pro price is also $19/user/mo) -- passthrough at AWS cost is the honest number until GCP exposes Code Assist seat pricing through the Billing Catalog API or a maintainer-curated contract-pricing table exists (same class of gap as Cloud Armor Enterprise, see the 'shield' rule above).
API Gateway -> Cloud Endpoints / Apigee; pricing model incompatible (per-call vs per-API); passthrough prevents LLM misroutes (observed: misrouted to Redis/Memorystore).
Step Functions -> Cloud Workflows; external transitions ($0.025/K transitions on AWS) map to Cloud Workflows steps ($0.01/K steps). Passthrough baseline until per-transition pricer built.
Step Functions (AmazonStepFunctions product alias) -> Cloud Workflows.
WAF -> Cloud Armor; multi-component (web ACL/hr + rule/mo + requests/M). Pricing model differs; passthrough baseline until per-component pricer built.

Shield Standard is free on GCP (Cloud Armor standard). Shield Advanced's flat $3,000/mo subscription -> Cloud Armor Enterprise Annual Subscription, priced dynamically by map_shield() (apply_static_mappings.py) against real catalog SKU EFB7-4299-A2EC ('Monthly Fee for Cloud Armor Enterprise Annual Subscription', service=Compute Engine, global, $3,000.00/mo flat -- exact list-price parity, both require a 1-year commitment tier). A prior version of this rule swept only the 'Networking'-service Cloud Armor Enterprise SKUs (Security Policy/Security Policy Rule/Requests -- all real but rate_usd=0.0, negotiated pricing) and wrongly concluded no priced SKU existed at all; the Annual Subscription base-fee SKU was missed because it lives under a different service (Compute Engine) in the catalog. mode=keep (not review) so this dynamic mapping isn't overwritten back to a flat passthrough stamp.
CloudFormation stack operations are free in GCP (Cloud Deployment Manager / Terraform is free open-source). $0 on GCP.
SSM Parameter Store -> Secret Manager (standard params free, advanced=$0.05/mo each). SSM Session Manager has no GCP equivalent charge. Passthrough.
SSM Parameter Store (advanced) -> Secret Manager ($0.06/version/mo vs $0.05/parameter/mo). Passthrough baseline.
EventBridge -> Pub/Sub or Eventarc; event routing pricing differs ($1/M events vs Pub/Sub throughput). Passthrough baseline.

CloudFront Security Savings Bundle is a flat-rate commitment bundling CDN + Shield Advanced + WAF into one line item -- there is no per-component split in the CUR to map separately, and no dedicated mapper exists for this bundle SKU (unlike ordinary CloudFront bandwidth/request rows, which do map to real Cloud CDN SKUs elsewhere). Nearest GCP equivalent confirmed via the same live catalog sweep used elsewhere in this pipeline (resolve_sku()/find-sku.sh against catalog.duckdb): Cloud CDN (bandwidth, already mapped for plain CloudFront rows) + Cloud Armor Enterprise (security tier, same-or-better than Shield Advanced -- sku_id B8E8-47B2-8B51 'Security Policy' $/mo, global). NOT dynamically SKU-priced here: that Cloud Armor Enterprise SKU's bundled-catalog rate is $0.00 (contract/negotiated pricing, not published via the Billing Catalog API -- see the 'shield' rule above for the same finding), so wiring a real gcp_sku_id would silently zero out this row's spend instead of pricing it. Passthrough at AWS cost is the honest number until a component-level, contract-price-aware pricer exists.

CloudFront -> Cloud CDN. Bandwidth rows are priced with dynamic destination-tier selection (Cloud CDN Cache Egress APAC/Americas/EMEA at $0.06-0.08/GB); per-request rows and Origin Shield are priced separately.

ACM public certs are free on both clouds (rows are usually $0, so passthrough = $0 anyway). ACM Private CA ($400/mo) has a GCP CAS equivalent — passthrough carries that real spend instead of hiding it at $0.
EKS cluster management fee ($0.10/hr/cluster) -> GKE Standard cluster fee ($0.10/hr, cost parity). Underlying EC2 node costs appear as separate EC2 line items.
ECS Fargate tasks -> GKE Autopilot pod capacity. ECS on EC2 nodes are billed as EC2 — those appear as separate EC2 line items.
Fargate vCPU/memory hours -> GKE Autopilot pod CPU/memory resources (directional estimate).

FaaS -> Cloud Run Functions (per invocation + GB-second memory & CPU components derived from the memory:vCPU ratio). Priced deterministically against real Cloud Run Functions rates where the bill format permits; otherwise resolved case-by-case with GCP billing catalog constraints.

Redis/Memcached -> Memorystore; priced by node GB + tier (GiB-hour formula, or an honest passthrough when node RAM/SKU can't be resolved). Verify cluster mode: ElastiCache Redis Cluster mode maps to Memorystore Redis Cluster (different SKU, 30-40% higher) — confidence held lower until cluster topology is confirmed.
DAX -> Memorystore for Redis.
MemoryDB (durable Redis) -> Memorystore for Redis. Observed misroute to Cloud SQL in past runs — this rule pins the correct target. Passthrough baseline; node-RAM pricer would improve it.
DAX -> Memorystore for Redis.
Key-value/doc -> Firestore (simple access patterns) or Bigtable (GSI-heavy / analytical). Target is workload-dependent; GSI-heavy DynamoDB requires re-architecture on GCP. Confidence capped at 50%.
Graph DB; no managed GCP equivalent — self-host or Spanner Graph.
Mongo-compatible; no managed GCP equivalent (MongoDB Atlas / Firestore).

AWS DMS billed per replication-instance-hour; GCP DMS billed per GiB of data copied ($2.08/GiB CDC in Mumbai, $0 for full dump). Ongoing CDC use (typical for $900+/mo spend) has real GCP cost but units are incompatible — passthrough until CDC data volume is known.

SageMaker -> Vertex AI (training/prediction/notebooks). Instance-hour pricing differs by accelerator and Vertex managed premium; passthrough baseline until a per-instance-type pricer exists. Kills observed 4-way target variance (echo/GCE/Manual/Vertex).
AWS Transfer Family (SFTP/FTPS/FTP) has no managed GCP equivalent — options are Storage Transfer Service (batch), SFTP on GCE, or third-party. Passthrough with manual-review flag.
SNS -> Pub/Sub.
SQS -> Pub/Sub.
SES has no native GCP equivalent (3rd-party/Workspace).

NFS file storage -> Cloud Filestore; priced per provisioned GB + tier (real per-tier Filestore capacity pricing, or an honest passthrough for Provisioned Throughput/IO rows with no Filestore equivalent).
AWS Managed AD -> Managed Service for Microsoft AD.
Native billing/reporting is free in GCP — likely $0.
KMS -> Cloud KMS (per key-version + operations).
-> Secret Manager (per secret-version + access).
Threat detection -> SCC Premium (different pricing model).

Amazon Inspector (per-resource vulnerability scanning: EC2/ECR/Lambda) -> SCC Premium (per-asset-under-management pricing); pricing models are structurally different (per-scan vs per-asset/mo), so carried as an honest passthrough rather than an invented rate -- same treatment as GuardDuty/Security Hub above.
VPC Endpoint -> Private Service Connect (per endpoint + data).
Transit Gateway -> NCC hub (per attachment + data).
VPN -> Cloud VPN (per tunnel-hour + egress).

AWS Client VPN is user-to-site remote-access VPN (billed per active connection-hour). GCP Cloud VPN is site-to-site IPsec (billed per always-on tunnel-hour) — a different product class that cannot serve the same purpose, so it is not used as the target here. GCP's nearest equivalent is zero-trust access via BeyondCorp Enterprise / IAP, which carries a different pricing model entirely. Passthrough at AWS cost pending manual review with the customer.
VPN -> Cloud VPN.
Resolver endpoints (DNS resolution/forwarding) != authoritative managed zone; needs Cloud DNS policies / hybrid DNS — architecture review.
Route 53 Resolver endpoint -> Cloud DNS forwarding, not a managed zone.

Route 53 Application Recovery Controller (ARC) is a multi-region failover control-plane (recovery cluster, routing controls, safety rules -- billed hourly, e.g. 'Global-Cluster-Hours') -- a fundamentally different product from plain Route 53 DNS, despite sharing the brand name. Confirmed via live catalog sweep: no GCP product matches this control-plane/cluster concept (Cloud DNS's only SKUs are 'DNS Query' and 'ManagedZone', a per-query/per-zone billing model that does not fit an hourly cluster fee at all -- a prior bug matched this row against the generic Route 53 rule below and priced its hourly quantity as if it were a DNS query count, producing a fabricated near-$0 GCP cost). Nearest conceptual equivalent would be a hand-built combination of Cloud DNS routing policies + health checks + Cloud Monitoring alerting, not a packaged, comparably-billed product -- passthrough at AWS cost is the honest number. Ordered before the generic 'route 53'/'route53' rules below so this specific product is never absorbed by the brand-name substring match.

Route 53 hosted zones ($0.50/zone/mo -> $0.20/zone/mo) and queries ($0.40/M ~ $0.40/M) -> Cloud DNS. Near-parity; passthrough baseline. Ordered AFTER resolver rules so resolver endpoints keep their specific target.
Route 53 (compact product alias) -> Cloud DNS.
Public IPv4 -> External IP charge (per IP-hour), exact per-IP-hour parity.
VPC in-use IPs -> External IP Charge; preserving flat_hourly mapper SKU.
